rationale: Two correctness gaps block the feature from working end-to-end: (1) user-initiated theme changes never call saveProfileSettings, so theme is effectively read-only from the backend — changes survive only until the next page load; (2) the onboarding migration path is broken for existing users because the 404 auto-create seeds completed:false and the fallback guard uses ?? which cannot reach localStorage when the backend value is a boolean false. Two additional major issues: a network-error path silently overwrites the user's actual theme with 'system', and four new Python source files are missing the required Apache 2.0 license headers. A later commit on this same branch/MR added AI Adoption Config persistence (reusing the existing dynamic_config key-value store), reviewed separately and folded in here: one critical finding (CR-007) — the serialized config exceeded the dynamic_config.value column's 10,000-char limit, so every PUT save would have failed — plus three major findings (CR-008: unguarded GET against corrupted persisted data; CR-009: uncaught TypeError on malformed PUT bodies surfacing as 500 instead of 400; CR-010: resetAiAdoptionConfig missing the loading/error state pattern saveAiAdoptionConfig has).

findings.title: User-initiated theme changes not saved to backend
findings.problem: setTheme() and applyTheme() write to localStorage but never call profileSettingsStore.saveProfileSettings(). Theme changes are stored in localStorage per-session only.
findings.impact: After the next page load, useInitialDataFetch calls applyBackendTheme with the unchanged backend value, overwriting any theme the user selected. Cross-device theme sync — the feature's main goal for the theme attribute — does not work.
findings.recommendation: In setTheme() (or applyTheme() gated on a flag), after writing to localStorage, call profileSettingsStore.saveProfileSettings(userId, { theme }) using the currently authenticated user's ID. The backend then becomes the source of truth and applyBackendTheme on next load will restore the correct theme.

findings.title: Existing users' onboarding completion state silently discarded on migration
findings.problem: The 404 auto-create path always seeds DEFAULT_PROFILE with onboarding.completed:false, ignoring localStorage ONBOARDING_COMPLETED_KEY. Additionally, isOnboardingCompleted() uses `profileSettings?.onboarding.completed ?? localStorage.getItem(...)` — when the backend record is loaded with completed:false, the nullish coalescing operator resolves to false (not to the localStorage value), making the fallback unreachable.
findings.impact: All users who completed onboarding before this migration will be shown the onboarding flow again on first load after deployment. The localStorage fallback code in isOnboardingCompleted/isFlowCompleted/isFirstPageVisit never executes once a backend record exists.
findings.recommendation: In the 404 auto-create path in fetchProfileSettings, read ONBOARDING_COMPLETED_KEY from localStorage before constructing DEFAULT_PROFILE and set completed:true if found. Also fix isOnboardingCompleted to avoid using ?? on a boolean: read profileSettings?.onboarding only when profileSettings is non-null, otherwise fall back.

findings.title: Non-404 fetch error stores DEFAULT_PROFILE, then overwrites user's actual theme
findings.problem: On any non-404 fetchProfileSettings failure, profileSettings is set to DEFAULT_PROFILE(userId) (theme:'system'). In useInitialDataFetch, backendTheme = profileSettings?.theme evaluates to 'system' (truthy), so applyBackendTheme('system') is called, replacing whatever theme the user had in localStorage.
findings.impact: A transient network error at startup silently resets the user's visible theme to 'system'. On subsequent loads the localStorage cache now reads 'system', and if the backend call succeeds, it returns the actual stored theme — an inconsistency that only resolves after a successful fetch.
findings.recommendation: When storing a fallback DEFAULT_PROFILE on error, do not store it in profileSettings (use a separate errorFallback flag or null-out the field). Alternatively, in useInitialDataFetch, only call applyBackendTheme when the profile was loaded from the backend successfully (not from the error path).

findings.title: Missing Apache 2.0 license headers on 4 new Python source files
findings.problem: user_profile_settings.py (model), user_profile_settings_repository.py, user_profile_settings_service.py, and user_profile_settings_router.py all start with `from __future__ import annotations` without the Apache 2.0 license comment block that all comparable existing source files (e.g. user_preferences_router.py) carry.
findings.impact: Violation of the project's code-quality standard, which requires Apache 2.0 headers on source files. This is a blocking standard per the project guide.
findings.recommendation: Add the standard Apache 2.0 license comment block (matching the header in user_preferences_router.py) to the top of all four files.

findings.title: saveProfileSettings propagates uncaught exceptions to awaited callers
findings.problem: saveProfileSettings has no try/catch. completeOnboarding and setViewedAppVersion await it; on PUT failure both surface an unhandled rejection with no user feedback or fallback local state update.
findings.impact: Completing onboarding or marking a release version viewed fails silently from the user's perspective but throws an error that may disrupt the call stack.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the PUT call in saveProfileSettings in a try/catch that logs the error and optionally re-throws for critical callers, or add error handling at each awaited call site.

findings.title: Fire-and-forget saveProfileSettings calls missing .catch() handlers
findings.problem: completeFlow, markPageVisited (onboarding.ts) and deleteRecentAssistant, updateRecentAssistants (assistants.ts) call saveProfileSettings without await and without .catch(). Any PUT failure produces a browser-visible unhandled promise rejection.
findings.impact: Silent failure telemetry noise; browsers may show console warnings or (in strict environments) escalate to unhandledrejection handlers.
findings.recommendation: Append .catch((e) => console.error('Failed to save profile settings', e)) to each fire-and-forget call.

findings.title: Serialized config exceeds DynamicConfig.value column limit — every save fails
findings.problem: save_ai_adoption_config() serializes config.to_dict() (the nested {value, description} shape) to JSON and passes it as the value to DynamicConfigService.aset(). Measured directly against the real AIAdoptionConfig defaults: json.dumps(config.to_dict()) is 12,758 characters, but DynamicConfig.value has max_length=10000 (SQLModel/Pydantic field constraint).
findings.impact: Every PUT save raises a Pydantic validation error before any DB write happens. The feature this ticket exists to fix — persisting admin edits — would not work at all; admins would see a 400/500 on every save attempt instead of a silent no-op, which is arguably worse than the original bug.
findings.recommendation: Serialize config.model_dump() (flat field values only, no verbose descriptions) for storage instead of config.to_dict() — verified directly: this produces 3,902 characters, comfortably under the limit. On read, reconstruct via AIAdoptionConfig(**json.loads(record.value)) instead of AIAdoptionConfig.from_dict(...), since the stored shape is now flat, not nested. Verified the round-trip (model_dump() -> json -> AIAdoptionConfig(**...) -> to_dict()) produces output identical to the original to_dict(). Apply this in both get_ai_adoption_config() and save_ai_adoption_config().

findings.title: Public GET has no guard against a corrupted or incompatible persisted record
findings.problem: get_ai_adoption_config() calls AIAdoptionConfig.from_dict(json.loads(record.value)) (or, after the CR-007 fix, AIAdoptionConfig(**...)) with no try/except when a record exists. A malformed stored value (corrupted JSON, or a shape mismatch after a future AIAdoptionConfig field change) raises an uncaught exception.
findings.impact: GET /v1/analytics/ai-adoption-config is documented and required to have no access control (public read). A single bad persisted value would break config retrieval for every user of the platform, not just admins, with no fallback — the None-record branch already has a safe default; the record-exists branch does not.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the persisted-record parse/reconstruct in try/except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError, TypeError), log a warning naming the corruption, and fall back to AIAdoptionConfig() defaults — mirroring the existing None-record branch's behavior exactly.

findings.title: Malformed PUT body (non-dict section value) raises uncaught TypeError, surfaces as 500 instead of 400
findings.problem: update_ai_adoption_config() calls AIAdoptionConfig.from_dict(request_body) directly with no schema validation on request_body: dict. Verified against config.py's _extract_value() helper: a body like {"ai_maturity": 5} causes "activation_threshold" not in 5 inside _extract_value, raising TypeError (not ValueError). handle_analytics_errors only maps ValueError to a clean 400 — TypeError falls into the generic except Exception branch, mapped to a 500.
findings.impact: An admin submitting a malformed (not just out-of-bounds) config gets a confusing 500 'Failed to retrieve AI adoption config' instead of an actionable 400 validation error. Also confirms a real, untested gap: the Testing Plan explicitly requires a 'PUT rejects out-of-bounds value (400)' test, and no test in the diff exercises either failure mode (structural or bounds).
findings.recommendation: Wrap AIAdoptionConfig.from_dict(request_body) in a local try/except (ValueError, TypeError) inside the route, re-raising as ExtendedHTTPException(400, ...) with a clear message. Add two tests: a structurally-malformed body (non-dict section) and an out-of-bounds value (e.g. a weight > 1.0), both asserting a 400 response.

findings.title: resetAiAdoptionConfig doesn't set loading/error state, unlike saveAiAdoptionConfig
findings.problem: saveAiAdoptionConfig sets this.loading[key]/this.error[key] around its api.put call and clears loading in a finally block. resetAiAdoptionConfig, changed in the same commit to call api.delete, does not — it only console.error's and rethrows on failure. Confirmed independently by two review lenses (blind and edge-case).
findings.impact: A failed reset shows no loading indicator and records no store-level error, unlike a failed save — an inconsistent UX for two closely related operations on the same settings page, and any UI relying on analyticsStore.error['ai-adoption-config'] to show a failure toast for reset would silently show nothing.
findings.recommendation: Mirror saveAiAdoptionConfig's loading/error/finally pattern in resetAiAdoptionConfig for consistency.
